Run the complete pre-commit workflow for xspct_hook and suggest a commit message.

## Steps (run in order — stop and report on failure)

### 1. Format
```bash
.venv/bin/ruff format src/ tests/
.venv/bin/ruff check --select I --fix src/ tests/
```
Report any files reformatted.

### 1.5 Remove AI code slop

Check the diff against main, and remove all AI generated slop introduced in this branch.

### 2. Lint
```bash
.venv/bin/ruff check src/ tests/
```
If there are lint errors, **stop** and report them. Do not proceed until the user resolves them.

### 3. pyrefly (strict preset, baseline applied)
```bash
.venv/bin/pyrefly check
```
Only findings missing from `.pyrefly-baseline.json` are reported. Do not update the baseline to hide
new findings. If you fixed baselined findings, run `.venv/bin/pyrefly check --prune-baseline` and
include the baseline change in the commit.
If there are type errors, **stop** and report them. Do not proceed until the user resolves them.

### 4. REUSE / SPDX compliance
```bash
.venv/bin/reuse lint
```
Every source file must have lines 1–2:
```
# SPDX-License-Identifier: EUPL-1.2
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: <year> Carsten Rosenberg <c.rosenberg@heinlein-support.de>
```
If reuse is not installed, scan manually for missing headers. Stop on violations.

### 5. Tests
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --tb=short
```
If any tests fail, **stop** and show the full failure output. Do not proceed.

### 6. Update changelog

Update `docs/changelog.md` with a new entry under `## Unreleased`, following the existing format.
Include all relevant changes since the last release, categorized by type (Features, Fixes,
Performance, etc.). Use bullet points for each change and ensure the formatting is consistent with
previous entries.

### 7. Stage formatted / fixed files
```bash
git add -u
```
List the files staged.

### 8. Suggest a commit message

Ask the user (or infer from the changes) what was done, then suggest a commit
message following [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/),
per `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the authoritative source — re-check it if these tables
go stale):

```
<type>(<scope>): <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New functionality |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `docs` | Documentation only |
| `refactor` | Restructuring without behavior change |
| `test` | Test-only change |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `build` | Build system, dependencies, `pyproject.toml` |
| `ci` | CI configuration |
| `chore` | Other maintenance |

Scopes: `protocol`, `wire`, `adapter`, `orchestrator`, `config`, `cli` (omit the scope for
`ci`/`build`/`docs`/`test`/`chore` changes that don't target one of these areas). Mark breaking
changes with `!` after the scope and/or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

Rules:
- Description in the imperative mood, lowercase, no trailing period.
- First line at most 72 characters.
- Independent changes go in separate commits — don't mix an adapter
  extension with a protocol-layer change in the same commit.

Example: `feat(wire): add native -01 registration endpoint`

### 9. GPG signing reminder

**ALL commits and tags must be GPG-signed:**
```bash
git commit -S -m "feat(wire): add native -01 registration endpoint"
git tag -s X.Y.Z -m "Tag message"
```
Remind the user to use `-S`.

## Hard rules

- **NEVER** include "generated by", "co-authored by", or any AI attribution in the commit message.
- Keep the commit message subject line under 72 characters.
- Use the imperative mood ("Add …", "Fix …", not "Added …" or "Fixes …").
